cells.tense: The work is going well right now, and the practice carries you without forcing.
cells.act: show someone the way you found
cells.ask: With one person who's still finding their way, name the step that opens the rest of this work — the place you keep returning to. Say it once, plainly, then stop there.
cells.core: You're building the new thing by hand, and the practice runs without forcing itself. The hours alone don't isolate you — they connect you to the work and, now, to someone in it. Solitude here is a workshop, not a wall. The time you've given this is the cost, and it's paid off. Keep what's working: take one route through the practice you know well and show it to someone still finding their way. Name the step that opens the rest, say it once, and stop there. Then the practice holds when you can't be the only one keeping it. What you show, they can use without you.
cells.sheetLine: Practice that flows points the way without forcing.
cells.verb: building something new through steady, skilled practice
cells.place: at the desk where the same work is done daily

cells.tense: You're braced for a future that refuses to be written in yet.
cells.act: cross over to the people it actually requires
cells.ask: Pick one person connected to this work and cross over to them — a message, a call, a knock — and say what ties you both to it. Not a progress report. The connection itself.
cells.core: On this build, you're pushing the work past the pace it can hold. Every unfinished piece becomes an emergency, every session gets audited. The practice starts to feel like something forced instead of something done. Refinement turns into a way to stay busy without sitting still. If it goes on, the work wears down the one person who has to keep at it — you. Cross over to someone it actually connects. Choose one person tied to this work and reach them before the next session: a message, a call, a knock, and say what ties you both to it. That pulls you out of the friction of working at the work and back into what the work is for.
cells.sheetLine: The push is outrunning the work it's meant to serve.
cells.verb: building something new through steady, skilled practice
cells.place: at the desk where the same work is done daily

cells.tense: You're still standing at the door that's already behind you.
cells.act: decide it and act the same day, without explaining
cells.ask: Decide the smallest next step for the work today and do it before the day ends. No announcement, no explanation. The doing speaks, or it doesn't.
cells.core: You're at the practice with no charge in it. The work gets done distantly, and the place at the desk empties while the intention stays elsewhere — in the last thing, in what should have been. The skill is real; the current is low. The way back moves forward, not inward. Decide the smallest next step for the work today and do it before the day ends. No explanation, no announcement. Let the doing be plain enough that it doesn't need defending. What's built comes back to the body that does it, one decision at a time, whether or not the charge is there yet.
cells.sheetLine: You're standing at the door with the current off.
cells.verb: building something new through steady, skilled practice
cells.place: at the desk where the same work is done daily

cells.tense: The pen is down, though you're already writing in this room.
cells.act: keep the heading when it is contested
cells.ask: The next time someone questions this build, hold your course without arguing for it. Do the work as planned. Let what you do answer, not the defense.
cells.core: This build has a keeper — the early hours, the repeated passes, the choice to remain with the material when it resists. Ask and you'd say the work just gets done. It isn't just getting done. It gets done by you, on purpose, and the hand doesn't count itself. Keep the heading when it's contested: the next time someone questions what you're building, hold your course without arguing for it. Do the work as planned and let what you do answer, not the defense. That's the whole act. What you chose stays chosen, and it's yours. Seeing it clearly is all the acknowledgment requires, and the work goes on without the credit.
cells.sheetLine: The practice is yours. Your word for it is routine.

A reader could reasonably say the practicing is so private it never becomes visible to anyone. The ask survives if the read is wrong: showing someone the route through your practice can be done by anyone at any stage. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is 'whatever you've found by staying with the work, you know how to point someone through.'
